provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My community
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list people in their community.
The pupils should be able to state the work of community members.

Introduction:
Last term we talked about family members.
Today we will talk about people in our community.

Content:
Community is where we live.
People in community are market women, teachers, drivers.
Market woman sells tomatoes at the market.
Teacher teaches us in school.
Driver drives danfo bus.

Class activity:
Pupils will stand up and name one community helper.

Evaluation questions:
Name one person in your community.
What does a teacher do?
Who sells things at the market?

Summary:
Our community has many people who help us.

topics.title: Helping one another
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to help at home.
The pupils should be able to tell a kindness story.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about people in our community.
Today we will learn how to help others.

Content:
Helping means doing good things for others.
At home we help sweep the floor.
At school we help friends pick up pencils.
Mama appreciates when we help.
Teacher smiles when we help.

Class activity:
Pupils will act out helping a friend who fell.

Evaluation questions:
How can you help at home?
What happens when you help others?
Tell one way to help at school.

Summary:
Helping others makes everyone happy.

topics.title: Obedience
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list people to obey.
The pupils should be able to explain why we obey.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about helping others.
Today we will learn about obedience.

Content:
Obedience means doing what elders say.
We obey parents and teachers.
We obey because they know what is best for us.
Mama says not to play on the road.
Teacher says not to run in class.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice obeying teacher's instructions quickly.

Evaluation questions:
Who should you obey?
Why do we obey teachers?
What happens if we don't obey?

Summary:
Obedience keeps us safe and happy.

topics.title: Punctuality
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the importance of coming early.
The pupils should be able to mention daily activities.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about obedience.
Today we will learn about punctuality.

Content:
Punctuality means coming on time.
We come to school early to learn well.
Our daily timetable has time for each thing.
Assembly time is 8 o'clock.
Class time starts after assembly.

Class activity:
Pupils will make a simple timetable for their day.

Evaluation questions:
What is punctuality?
Why should we come to school early?
What time does school start?

Summary:
Coming on time helps us learn better.

topics.title: Cleanliness is next to Godliness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to keep clean.
The pupils should be able to list clean body parts.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about punctuality.
Today we will learn about cleanliness.

Content:
Cleanliness means keeping ourselves and things clean.
We wash our face with water every morning.
We wear clean clothes to school.
We sweep the class to keep it clean.
Dirty things can make us sick.

Class activity:
Pupils will wash their hands with soap and water.

Evaluation questions:
How do you keep your body clean?
What should you wear to school?
Why is cleanliness important?

Summary:
Keeping clean keeps us healthy.

topics.title: Care of public things
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name public things in school.
The pupils should be able to explain how to care for them.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about cleanliness.
Today we will learn about caring for public things.

Content:
Public things belong to everyone.
In school we have desks, fans, and toilets.
We should not write on desks.
We should not break chairs.
We should keep toilets clean for everyone.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice sitting properly on chairs.

Evaluation questions:
Name one public thing in school.
How should we use desks?
Why should we keep toilets clean?

Summary:
We all must take care of public things.

topics.title: The national anthem
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the national anthem.
The pupils should be able to state one line meaning.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about caring for public things.
Today we will learn the national anthem.

Content:
The national anthem is Nigeria's song.
We sing it to show love for our country.
Nigeria our homeland.
We stand up straight when we sing.
We sing with our friends in school.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice singing the anthem with actions.

Evaluation questions:
What is the national anthem?
How do we show respect when singing?
What does Nigeria our homeland mean?

Summary:
The national anthem shows our love for Nigeria.

topics.title: The national pledge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the national pledge.
The pupils should be able to explain one part of it.

Introduction:
Last week we learned the national anthem.
Today we will learn the national pledge.

Content:
The national pledge is our promise to Nigeria.
We say it with our right hand on our chest.
We promise to be loyal and honest.
We promise to serve Nigeria well.
We say it in the morning assembly.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice saying the pledge together.

Evaluation questions:
What is the national pledge?
How do we say the pledge?
What do we promise in the pledge?

Summary:
The pledge is our promise to Nigeria.

topics.title: Being a good pupil
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to be good pupils.
The pupils should be able to explain why respect matters.

Introduction:
Last week we learned the national pledge.
Today we will learn how to be good pupils.

Content:
A good pupil works hard in class.
A good pupil respects teachers and friends.
We follow class rules to keep peace.
We raise our hands before speaking.
We do not fight with others.

Class activity:
Pupils will demonstrate good behavior in class.

Evaluation questions:
How can you be a good pupil?
Why should you respect teachers?
What are class rules?

Summary:
Being good helps everyone learn well.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term work.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate learned values.

Introduction:
This week we will revise what we learned this term.
We will play a game to show what we know.

Content:
We learned about community and helping others.
We learned about obedience and punctuality.
We learned about cleanliness and caring for things.
We learned the national anthem and pledge.
We learned how to be good pupils.

Class activity:
Pupils will play a quiz game in teams.

Evaluation questions:
What does obedience mean?
How do you help at home?
What is the national anthem?

Summary:
Let's remember all we learned this term.
